purpose: Teach: 芥川/ビルマ/ベネズエラ/茅ヶ崎/ナイロビ/鈴鹿/ホノルル/テレビ東京

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、国語で芥川龍之介習ったろ?
lines.en: Riku, you studied Akutagawa Ryunosuke in literature class, didn't you?
lines.style: Light, teasing challenge. Leans in with a small smile. Testing what he'll do with it. Pace steady—she knows exactly what she's doing.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、社会でビルマ習ったろ?桜
lines.en: You learned about Burma in social studies, didn't you, Sakura?
lines.style: Mirrors her energy back at her with equal measure. Amused but not conceding. Eyes bright. Playing the same game she started.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、ベネズエラの社会問題勉強したな
lines.en: Riku, you studied Venezuela's social issues, didn't you?
lines.style: Slight uptick in intensity—pressing harder. Quick, pointed delivery. Testing if he'll keep up or crack.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、茅ヶ崎の海でサーフィンしたな、桜
lines.en: You went surfing at Chigasaki Beach, didn't you, Sakura?
lines.style: Same measured rhythm back. Not rushing. A small half-smile in the voice. He's enjoying this—the back-and-forth without stakes.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、修学旅行でナイロビ行ったろ?
lines.en: Riku, you went to Nairobi on your school trip, didn't you?
lines.style: Escalating again—voice lifts slightly. Accusatory without bite. This one feels bigger; she's watching for his reaction.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、鈴鹿サーキット行きたがってたな、桜
lines.en: You wanted to go to Suzuka Circuit, didn't you, Sakura?
lines.style: Firmer now. The challenge is clearer. Direct eye contact in the voice. Still playful but the edge is sharper.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: リク、お前、ホノルルマラソン憧れてたな
lines.en: Riku, you admired the Honolulu Marathon, didn't you?
lines.style: Breath before the punch. The sentence lands with real weight now. She's naming something that matters—watching his face.

lines.speaker: riku_teen
lines.jp: お前、テレビ東京のアニメ観てたな、桜
lines.en: You used to watch TV Tokyo anime, didn't you, Sakura?
lines.style: Quieter. The game has shifted. He's turned it inward—naming something real about her. Close and careful. Not playful anymore; honest.
